definitions.explanation: The mechanical device in a camera that controls exposure time by opening and closing to allow light onto the film or sensor.
A metal or wooden door that rolls down or folds to close a storefront, garage, or window.

examples.english: To press the shutter (take a photo).

examples.japanese: シャッタースピードを{調整|ちょうせい}する。
{店|みせ}のシャッターが{閉|し}まっていた。
シャッター{街|がい}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: There are more and more shuttered shopping streets.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: From English "shutter."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・シャッターを{切|き}る (to press the shutter, take a photo)
・シャッターを{押|お}す (to press the shutter)
・シャッタースピード (shutter speed)
・シャッターチャンス (photo opportunity)
・シャッターを{下|お}ろす (to close the shutter/rolling door)
・シャッターを{上|あ}げる (to open the shutter/rolling door)

SOCIAL CONTEXT: シャッター{街|がい} (shuttered shopping street) and シャッター{通|どお}り (shuttered street) are terms describing the decline of local shopping districts where many stores have permanently closed, a common sight in rural Japan due to population decline and competition from large retailers.

RELATED TERMS:
・ピント - focus (photography)
・{露出|ろしゅつ} - exposure
・{雨戸|あまど} - traditional wooden storm shutters
